sections.title: How does the Gas vs electric dryer calculator work?
sections.html:
The Gas vs electric dryer calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports wattage (Electric dryer) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the electricity consumption, the unit electricity cost, the drying cost (Electric dryer) and the gas rating.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Gas vs electric dryer calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Wattage=electricity consumption ÷ time per drying cycle
Drying loads per week=drying cost ÷ (unit electricity cost × electricity consumption)
Drying cost per year=52 × drying cost
Wattage=electricity consumption per load ÷ time per drying cycle
Time per drying cycle=gas consumption ÷ gas rating
Drying loads per week=drying cost ÷ (unit electricity cost × electricity consumption per load + unit gas cost × gas consumption)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Time per drying cycle = 10 min, Wattage = 3000 kW, Electricity consumption = 10 kWh and Unit electricity cost = 0.12. Working through the relationship above gives Electricity consumption per load = 12906.31 kWh and Gas consumption = 55479.924 kWh.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Electricity consumption per load = 12906.31 kWh and Gas consumption = 55479.924 kWh should be roughly the size you expected from Time per drying cycle = 10 min and Wattage = 3000 kW.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Gas vs electric dryer calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the electricity consumption, the unit electricity cost and the drying cost — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Gas vs electric dryer calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns wattage (Electric dryer), derived from the electricity consumption, the unit electricity cost and the drying cost. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Gas vs electric dryer calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the electricity consumption, the unit electricity cost, the drying cost and the gas rating, which is 7 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter time per drying cycle in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Time per drying cycle opens in minutes and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Electricity consumption per load = 12906.31 kWh. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Gas vs electric dryer calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
